text_fidelity_a:
My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set This is a fun little train set for toddlers. The current product image is misleading, however, so I've posted photos to show how this nice little set comes. It comes in a handy carry bag with large plastic track pieces and two toys: Thomas the Tank Engine and Harold the Helicopter. Not quite sure why they include a helicopter to roll around a train track, but I suppose he is one of the more popular characters in Thomas' world. Regardless, they are both cute and large enough for a toddler to get his hands on and push around the track.

Thomas and Harold come attached to a piece of cardboard which keeps them in place. Before you go crazy on how to get these off - after a bit of struggling myself, I realized that all you have to do is rotate the plastic tab things that are holding them in place (located on the bottom). Just turn the tabs 90 degrees (doesn't matter which way) to free Thomas and Harold.

You will definitely need to help your put this together as the track pieces have a snug fit. they may loosen with time, however. There are instructions on how to put the track together, though I'm sure you can figure out your own unique layouts as well. The bridge pieces need a special little twist to put them together and remove them, so pay attention to that in the instructions, otherwise the rest simply snap together as you'd expect.

This is a really fun little set with a a nice carry bag to store all the pieces and even take the set with you on adventures. Little ones will love it!
text_fidelity_b: My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set

text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Beyblade Metal Masters Triple Battle Set Action Figure This toy is basically (for those not familiar) a couple of spinning tops that one sets in motion in a thin plastic 'stadium'. The middle of the floor of the stadium is an interchangeable disc with grooves that the tops can fall into in order to get some crazy spinning going. This was tested and played with by a few kids, ages 7 to 12. One was already familiar with this Beyblade series, he told me his got 'stomped on and broken' by another kid, and one can see how that would be easy. The stadium, which keeps the spinning 'tops' from going all over the house, is pretty flimsy. Maybe that's a good thing for careful kids. Out of the box I thought they would be bored pretty quick, but not so! We quickly abandoned the book of rules and started making our own. Best of all, the instructions were so easy, the 10 year old assembled everything. This was pretty major, as he has dexterity issues. This toy was perfect for him. I even sat on the floor and played a few games. Another nice thing about it is that it's good for all ages (over 8 as the box states) as there is an element of luck, thus insuring some wins from younger kids.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Beyblade Metal Masters Triple Battle Set Action Figure

SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop A simple way to amuse and practice your shot, the SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop offers glow in the dark appeal, easy assembly, and hours of fun. It hooks on the top of most doors so you can lie in bed and practice shooting or attach it to your office door at work for some quick stress relief.

Out of the box, this basketball hoop requires some assembly, but it shouldn’t take long to attach the parts and prep it for use. The hooks that attach it to a door are not adjustable, but they are designed to fit a wide range of door thicknesses. After attaching, you may notice that it lacks stability. I noticed it, too, but I also found that it didn’t matter. It doesn’t need to be completely stable because the weight of the included basketball is so light. Throw after throw results in no bouncing or other movement for me, so don’t worry if the hoop seems less secure than you would prefer. Unless your door is very thin, it should be fine.

Once you have the ball inflated, the toy is ready for use. You may want to set everything in direct light for a few hours at first, to help with the glowing. If you don’t, then the glow will be very faint. Still, it should be enough to make it visible in the dark so that, if you use this at home, you or your kids can see it in the dark and play before you fall asleep. One thing that new buyers need to realize is that, due to the thickness of the hooks, it may not be possible to close the door to which this is attached. My door won’t close, but I attached it to a door that normally stays open all of the time anyway. If your door won’t close with this attached, then you will have no choice but to go back and forth, taking it down and putting it back up.

Overall, this seems like a good toy and it should be fun for the basketball enthusiast in your home. There is no glass and the construction is made to last. The glow in the dark feature could be better, but other than that, it seems like an entertaining way to pass the time.
text_fidelity_b: SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures Doll & Accessories, Travel Set with Daisy Doll, Kitten, Working Suitcase & 9 Pieces (Amazon Exclusive) The Barbies in my day were just ridiculously shaped, so much so that even in the third grade I rejected them as a model that I would never live up to in my own feminine figure. I remember wishing that I could play with Barbies, but the body shapes made me feel unhappy and inadequate – you might think girls aren't aware of this kind of thing at a young age, but I certainly was. I owned one or two, but they were never something I love for this reason.

So just imagine my delight to realize that Barbie has created so many interesting and diverse dolls now to play with. This Daisy figure has really just a normal kind of shape that you would see on many, many ladies and moms at the grocery store. She looked beautiful, and also has a much more realistic form. I love the styling of her outfit, and her gorgeous pink hair just straight up makes me happy to look at and brush.

The way that they chose to craft Barbies slightly bigger thighs was interesting to me, so I took a photo of it. Overall, this feels like a really body positive, average pretty Barbie to play with, who is stylish and fun and attractive yet doesn't set up my daughter with completely ridiculous ideas of what women might look like.

Even the normal Barbies, I have a chicken farmer Barbie, and a Barbie who runs a doggy daycare, seem like their proportions have evolved somewhat, and then the fact that they are doing normal things like cleaning up dog messes and collecting eggs really goes so far in my book. I also love the Ken doll who is doing his own laundry in his very own washing machine. My husband is a little flummoxed by my absolute flat out glee at seeing such a thing, but I think setting the expectation that Ken will enjoy doing his own self-care chores is an excellent one for young ladies.

Overall, from having the impression that I would never let my children play with Barbies, I've come a long way, and that's because Barbie has come a long way to. I'm delighted with Daisy, and her cool accessories and great look.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures Doll & Accessories, Travel Set with Daisy Doll, Kitten, Working Suitcase & 9 Pieces (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder These products, both the dry float lounger and the socializer are prime examples of why I test products the way I do prior to writing my review.

When I initially received these products and inflated them I was fairly impressed with the design and comfort - by 18 days later both were flat lumps of rubber in the trash.

First the socializer never held air. After inflation by the following morning it had deflated to around 70% capacity. I put it under water in the pool and discovered multiple small defects in 2 seams.

The dry float lounger lasted a bit longer at 18 days but then was found flat due to a separation at the seam.

It is important to note neither of these were ever used by children or in any rough play as when I review products I adhere to strict guidelines - and there are no children in the home.

While the socializer is listed as a dry float it appears the user’s calves and feet would be in the water. The lounger pool float is perfect for those who prefer to float completely out of the water. When floating on this no part of the body is submerged in the water.

While 88-90% of the world’s population is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the cup holder on the left side and made it too small to hold a standard 12 Oz can for both of these floats. This is simply poor designing.

While these floats come with a small patch kit, these are only helpful when repairing a puncture and absolutely will not hold a torn seam.

While these floats appeared to have promise initially, in well under a month they proved to be poorly designed, and of substandard construction and materials.

I would not recommend either of these products.
text_fidelity_b: Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder

PRO’s: width and length of slide (twice as long as other slides in target audience), easy setup/operate/put away, splash zone (pool at end) works to stop toddlers. CON’s: the streaming water that “wets” the slide is too wide near the end of the slide and hardly existing at the start of the slide. A simple design improvement would be to have far less watering holes for the slip and slide near the splash zone and progressively more as you near the starting point. This to be is the largest flaw in the slide.

GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa Impressive shower head at an impressive price. Let's break it down...

** IN THE BOX ** Along with the showerhead there is a small roll of teflon thread tape, rubber pipe gasket, in-pipe flow restrictor, and instructions.

** INSTALLATION ** Remove old shower head. Clean pipe threads. Apply 3 turns of pipe thread in a CLOCKWISE direction. Extend shower head extension pipe arm all the way out. If you want flow restriction, insert now, other insert pipe gasket. Attach shower head in a CLOCKWISE direction by hand until tight. Cover the plastic thread cap (nearest the pipe) with a cloth and tighten 1/4 turn with a pliers or pipe wrench using GENTLE pressure. The shower head can now be straightened by gentle turning the adjustment screw (nearest shower head) by hand. It will click. Once you have the general downward direction of the shower head placed, test for leaks. If it leaks at the pipe & shower head connection, gently tighten another 1/4 turn. Once you're ready you can position the shower head, by head, any which way you like . It will click letting you know it's locked.

** USAGE ** Turn water on to your favorite temperature and insert your glorious naked self under the shower head. Look up at the nipples. Yes, there are 90 nipples up there. Very supple nipples that can be squeezed for cleaning. With so many nipples I don't think I'm ever leaving the shower ever again. The 90 nipples provided me an even pressurized rain all over my smelly carcass.

** THOUGHTS ** The TH2.5 works like a charm. Big, even rain all over me. Just what I wanted. Installation was simple provided you have normal shower pipes and are a bit handy with some pliers. The joints articulate well with no movement once set. The joints, once set, should accommodate short and tall humans. I'm 6'1", the wild redhead is 5'7" so this head works amazingly well for both of us. Did I mention there were 90 nipples?

** POINTS OF INTEREST **
- flow is optional and NOT installed
- joints articulate with a solid 'click' and stay in place
- pipe tape and gasket are included
- cover with cloth during final tightening to avoid scratching
- gently squeeze the nipples to clean
- looks like the USS Enterprise from the side... Aye, Aye Captain!
- I just love saying the word 'nipples'
text_fidelity_b: GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces) The first thing I noticed about this set was the weight. This is the first LEGO set that I've gotten that I would actually describe as heavy. That's a lot of brick. The box is nice, and contains several smaller boxes. Those boxes have some blueprint art on them, but no useful labeling as to where to begin. You need to open them all anyway, because the unlabeled bags of large parts are mixed in with some of the later bags, despite being needed early on. The bag numbering only goes up to about 20, but there are many bags for each number and the bags have bags in them. The instruction book is huge and spiral bound, with some nice history in the early pages.

The set goes together surprisingly quickly early on, starting with the display base and docking clamps, which the ship is built on, with sections being build and then clipped on. The internal support structure is well engineered and solid. You get a good impression of the overall size and shape of the ship by the time you are done with bag 2.

At first glance, this may look like a tedious grey set where all the parts look the same, but the insides are brightly colored. This is really nice because the parts being built are often rotated between panels, and the colors really help with both finding the parts and orienting with the instructions. When you're done, it also makes it easy to spot anything you missed, because the grey exterior will have rainbow colors there.

One disappointment is the thin area down the sides of the ship. I like them fine individually, but the instructions have you build them identically, so rather than being bilaterally symmetrical, one side looks like it's upside down compared to the other. I understand this saved them some pages, and made construction a little easier, but I would've appreciated a heads up so I could build it mirrored, since I think that would've worked out fine, at least for the greebles on the outside. I may actually take one side apart and redo it, though It's the kind of detail that an observer might not notice because this thing is so big. There are other areas that are more obviously asymmetrical, which is true to the movie, but looks really jarring to me the way they implemented it.

After completing it, I feel like it was designed by two different teams of people. The interior structure is an awesome feat of engineering, and so sturdy you can carry the whole thing by an interior handle, despite its great weight, and they did it with all existing parts. The exterior is about as expected in a Lego set. The transition between the two is weak. Brushing against it risks knocking things off. Sometimes it's just some barely attached pieces on the back, other times something obviously comes apart inside that's going to take some doing to get to and fix. The different sections are often just resting loosely on each other and sometimes look uneven. There is a tiny and comically inadequate clip to hold the four sections of the front in alignment. You may want to think about what you're going to do with it when it's done. It's large, heavy, and oddly shaped. Comes on a nice stand though.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge Well first, this game is absolutely ridiculous. Some of the challenges with the hands are near to impossible. But it did exactly what we hoping for at our last family reunion. It got several families blended into the fun and laughing hysterically, even those who had just driven 12 hours. The premise is easy, you have to do everything with Tiny or Tinier fake hands from catching a ball to acting out charades. The rules are simple although the rules of betting and scoring were less than clear to us. To be honest, we pretty much abandoned the betting and scoring of each round and just played the cards and the spinner. In the end we just declared the kids the winners.

Some things we learned.
- Put the score card well out of harms way. Ours was trod upon and score pieces were constantly tossed around.
- You cannot hold onto a pen with the hands like a baseball bat and swing it without impaling someone with the pen
- Give yourself lots of room
- The Charades part went over best.

Not sure how often this will come out, but it is a great leveler of ages and abilities and plays well in groups as long as kids are eight and up. It is kinetic, laugh producing and fun.

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Silver There have been a number of games based on the the concept of the Golf card game. Like that game, the point of this game is to have the lowest amount of points in your hand while having a number of blind cards that may be high or low. So you need to replace them while possibly and accidentally passing a great card to the next player in the discard pile. Much like Golf, once you think you have the best hand, you call and end to the game and everyone gets one more round to try to improve them hands. If you are lowest, you get zero points, if you are not, you take a penalty.

So that is the basic idea behind the game, but from there, there are many twists to make the game more interesting. Each card has a secret ability to allow you to see the other card in your village (hand.) Also, there is a mechanism to remove duplicate cards which allows you to quickly dump a lot of points from your hand (village.)

The cards are very nice, the amulet is also nice and allows you to lock a great card so that neither you or others can mess with it. The box could be a lot smaller, basically this is a deck game with a single piece for locking a card. you could put it into a box for a pack of hoyles cards.

All in all, an interesting twist on a classic card game concept.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Silver

Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions I am always looking for fun games that my family and I can enjoy together on game night and having not heard of Selfie I decided to give it a shot. It is a fun game but seems based on some other popular games that have been around for a while.

“Selfie” could just have easily been called “Apples to Apples Meets Charades!” which is a fairly concise way to describe it. Each player is dealt a set of cards describing a scenario where one would make some kind of facial expression, and then takes a selfie shot of that expression. After looking at the selfie shot, everyone else then plays one of their own cards to describe the expression, from which the original player selects a winner he/she likes most. Each person takes a turn taking a selfie and selecting others’ cards.

The game can be played without a phone or camera but it’s a lot easier with such a device which will help eliminate disagreements.

It should be obvious that this is not a game for the self-conscious individual.

Though I don’t think this game is all that original, it is a fun game and works in a crowd. This is the kind of game to break out during a party in the dorms or on a Saturday night with the family. It’s fun, gameplay is lively and fast-paced.

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

The pieces are interesting, especially the light up one, and they are made of nice, sturdy plastic. But there are a few issues that make this toy frustrating for my kids to play with.

The biggest problem is that the pieces do not have consistent tolerances for the connecting portions. Sometimes they snap together easily while other times it takes a lot of force. My 2 and 4 year olds cannot do this without help. They always end up knocking the sections over when trying to put the pieces together. This hasn’t been the issue when they played with another brands’ marble run.

Another issue is that there are not enough base pieces compared to the number of “action” pieces (like the ramps, slides, etc). This results in having to build tall, unstable designs that are easily knocked over, which makes the first problem even worse.

Also, the piece that shoots the marbles up is difficult for my fairly coordinated 4 year old to use. It requires a quick tap that is firm but not too hard. It would be nice if it was easier to use. Both of my kids like the idea of this piece, but I end up having to do it for them. And I can’t always get this piece to shoot the marble properly every time.

Last, it would have been nice to have a couple of example layouts included in the instructions. This is not too big of a deal, but the pieces are difficult to connect and take apart, so for my kids’ sake, knowing some layouts that use the different sections properly would be nice.

Activity tables, in general, have always been a huge hit with all of our babies, but this one is more unique in the sense that it encourages a lot of pounding. I love and prefer it because it's better for the environment... but it isn't very visually gift friendly. This fire station is almost entirely plastic, except for one small area. Yes, it is apparently a high-quality plastic, but it is still plastic. Wooden toys are sturdy and made to last across multiple generations. Plastic is not.

I personally think that, since this toy set is made of plastic, it is quite overpriced and not a good value. It is priced as if it were made of wood. Further, I wonder why on earth a company that is famed for its high-quality, wooden toys would opt to convert to plastic toys? It makes no sense.

However, if you are not looking for wooden toys for your child or grandchild, the fact that this is just another plastic toy set, in a world already over-filled with plastic, the plastic construction may not bother you. This toy set, on the positive side, does have very attractive, bright colors, and it does inspire creative play, as the older, wooden sets did. It's just not wood!

This set is for children age 3 and up because of small parts and a choking hazard.

It's battery-operated and the nailbiting action of wondering whether your car is going to make it through an up to do the trick makes it exciting for the kids to continue testing it.

I found it a giant pain to put together, and usually with hot wheels I would take them apart and put them back together so we can store them when not in use, but this one kind of broke my brain on the putting it back together part, so we just let it take up a good portion of our living room all the time.
